question: Do general_element_part, routine_name, and general_element account for a material share of prediction cost on the production tail?
hypothesis: The three retained hot rules dominate adaptive prediction on the highest-cost files, with routine_name and general_element causing substantial LL fallback and ambiguity.
selection: 12 opaque files with the highest median TypeScript parser-core time in experiment 003
acceptance: Only opaque file identities and hashes leave the private corpus.
Prediction time, invocations, SLL/LL transitions, LL fallback, and ambiguity are reported for all three target rules.
Profile build/setup time is excluded from the in-container parser profile elapsed time.
limitations: Profiling instrumentation changes absolute runtime; use shares and event counts, not unprofiled wall-time comparison.
The selection is intentionally tail-biased and does not estimate whole-corpus rule shares.
Java uses the unmodified upstream target while the production candidate is TypeScript with local adaptations.
